Both observed-maximum fields remain initialized to all ones (`0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`), and the dedicated power rail cannot yet be documented as an approved mitigation because full empirical qualification remains pending. The loaded execution field remains unpopulated because no stress campaign has yet been executed on this machine. Populating this value requires running the factorial contention campaign of @sec-placement-testing-separation directly on physical hardware. In that campaign, the discrete microcontroller executes its safety loop while the host application processor saturates neural accelerator clusters with trajectory proposals and writes continuous trace logs at maximum junction temperature, triggering the refusal branch across stress trials. Every cycle time recorded during this contention benchmark must remain at or below the declared worst-case execution time, $T_{\text{wcet}} =$ `{python} PlacementMachine.wcet_str`. Furthermore, the onset of powered deceleration, timed from the arrival of the last valid trajectory renewal, must occur within `{python} PlacementSeparationBudget.renewal_to_onset_str`. Until physical instrumentation confirms these bounds, the permission-independence claims of the safety case rest on unverified assertions, preventing any deployment safety release.

The external test ledger inventories all shared silicon and platform resources: memory channels, cache partitions, DMA engines, and power rails, alongside every competing bus master. For each resource, the ledger documents the hardware arbitration configuration and the resulting contention latency. For the safety permission rail, it records the selected `{python} PlacementMachine.rail_holdup_str` hold-up capacitance and its pending qualification by a supply-loss fault-injection campaign. The ledger also formalizes the electrical isolation boundary by enumerating allowable rail claimants, restricting access strictly to the microcontroller, the gate-drive logic, and the spring-applied brake release coils, while entirely excluding unverified proposal-side compute loads.

Any contention measurement is meaningful only in the context of its exact operating state. The test ledger therefore qualifies each latency distribution with cryptographic hashes of the active neural model and system firmware, DVFS policies, enclosure thermal interface materials, ambient and junction temperatures, power rail voltages, interconnect arbitration weights, synthetic traffic generation profiles, sensor sampling rates, measurement instrumentation calibration, sample counts, and total test duration. The ledger records these parameters alongside full latency histograms and explicit enumerations of unexercised operational states, while the fixed header exposes only the scalar maxima for fast verification. For example, the $10^7$-tick trace evaluated in @sec-placement-testing-separation spans only `{python} PlacementSeparationBudget.trace_h_str` h `{python} PlacementSeparationBudget.trace_min_str` min `{python} PlacementSeparationBudget.trace_sec_str` s of operation on a single physical machine. Such exposure demonstrates that the system survived specific benchmark conditions, but it does not exclude rare multi-contender collisions or provide a statistical bound across an entire production fleet.

Every placement record entry requires a predeclared falsification criterion formulated before executing hardware tests. This criterion defines the physical boundary that constitutes architectural failure, such as any safety enforcement cycle exceeding the declared `{python} PlacementMachine.wcet_str` worst case during concurrent neural accelerator bursts and DMA transfers\index{DMA}. The record documents the empirical execution distribution against this criterion and registers whether the isolation hypothesis survived or failed. When contention violates the latency budget and necessitates architectural revision, the record details the specific mitigation deployed, such as configuring bandwidth throttling on the neural accelerator memory bus. Furthermore, the test entry must explicitly report boundary conditions left unexercised during the test run, such as operating temperatures above the `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.t_ambient_str` $^{\circ}\text{C}$ bay ambient, multi-bit error injection in tightly coupled memory, or cascading sensor transceiver failures.

@Sec-verification consumes the documented arbitration points and shared power rails as a target map for hardware and software fault injection\index{Fault Injection}, deliberately corrupting shared structures to test whether fault containment matches predicted isolation domains. @Sec-release incorporates the verified execution bounds and unexercised operational limits into the formal safety case\index{Safety Case}, transforming raw physical measurements into auditable evidentiary warrants for real-world deployment.

With the placement record in place, the stopping budget is specified row by row for a wheeled mobile manipulator whose resident fallback is a brake-to-stop suffix on stable ground. A budget developed for one embodiment earns trust as a method only if it survives a machine with different dynamics. A legged humanoid, whose fallback trajectory must dynamically sustain balance while traversing unstructured terrain, provides the most demanding stress test of these principles (\ref{capstone-placement-humanoid-crucible}).

```{python}
#| label: calc-placement-humanoid-offset
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ PART III CAPSTONE: A CAMERA-IMU OFFSET ON A TURNING HEAD
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-placement-hardware-allocation (capstone-placement-humanoid-crucible)
# │
# │ Goal: Show that the observation-age row of the stopping budget survives on
# │       a biped: an uncalibrated camera-IMU offset during a head turn
# │       misplaces a point just as information age displaces a moving base.
# │ Show: 10 ms at 1.5 rad/s misplaces a point at 5 m by 7.5 cm.
# │ How: calc_spatial_information_age_displacement with the point's tangential
# │      speed omega * r; the three inputs are scenario assumptions.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim.core.units import millisecond, meter, second, ureg
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import calc_spatial_information_age_displacement
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_latency, fmt_length, check

class HumanoidOffset:
    # ┌── 1. LOAD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    offset = 10 * millisecond  # scenario assumption; category: illustrative (uncalibrated camera-IMU offset)
    omega = 1.5 * ureg.radian / second  # scenario assumption; category: illustrative (head turn rate)
    lookahead = 5.0 * meter  # scenario assumption; category: illustrative (range to the point)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    v_tangential = (omega * lookahead).to(meter / second)
    displacement = calc_spatial_information_age_displacement(v_tangential, offset).to(ureg.centimeter)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(displacement.magnitude - 7.5) < 1e-9, "Canon: 10 ms at 1.5 rad/s misplaces a point at 5 m by 7.5 cm.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    offset_str = fmt_latency(offset, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    omega_str = fmt(omega.to(ureg.radian / second).magnitude, precision=1)
    lookahead_str = fmt_length(lookahead, unit=meter, precision=0)
    displacement_str = fmt_length(displacement, unit=ureg.centimeter, precision=1)
```

::: {#capstone-placement-humanoid-crucible .callout-perspective title="When the fallback is a step"}
**Question**: Which rows of the stopping budget survive when the fallback is a step rather than a stop?

When hardware placement guarantees deterministic execution for the single control cycle quantified by $\tau_{\text{delay}}$, the stopping-budget framework applies directly to the mobile manipulator's powered braking maneuver, with dispatch-to-admission delay allocated and drive-energy qualification still open. However, a bipedal humanoid walking mid-stride possesses no stationary equilibrium into which it can instantaneously brake. Its fallback maneuver is dynamic, a recovery step. Every row of the stopping budget must consequently be re-evaluated for dynamic stepping:

* **Observation age survives.** Temporal latency continues to translate directly into spatial displacement, the conversion stated in @sec-perception-age-budget. On an articulated sensor head undergoing angular rotation, this error scales with viewing distance: a feature at range $r$ traverses space at tangential speed $v_{\text{tangential}} = \omega r$ under an angular rate $\omega$. For instance, an uncalibrated `{python} HumanoidOffset.offset_str` camera–IMU temporal offset during a `{python} HumanoidOffset.omega_str` rad/s head pan misidentifies the position of an obstacle located `{python} HumanoidOffset.lookahead_str` ahead by `{python} HumanoidOffset.displacement_str`.
* **Commitment semantics change.** The latched zero-velocity trajectory suffix established in @sec-planning-behavior-seam is replaced by a certified recovery stepping trajectory. Rather than terminating in a stationary rest configuration, this contingency plan must be admitted alongside the nominal motion command to guarantee safe placement of the swing foot onto an admissible support polygon.
* **The safety inset changes.** The geometric obstacle clearance margins derived in @sec-enforcement-safe-sets-conditional-permission no longer suffice to guarantee dynamic balance. A recovery step demands full closed-loop hybrid dynamics, relative-degree constraint analysis, identification of reachable capture regions, and actuation limits under torque saturation. Kinematic tracking uncertainty and ground reaction force disturbances must propagate directly into this forward invariance set before a valid safety inset can be calculated.
* **The placement record expands.** Because commanding zero joint velocity mid-stride causes immediate instability rather than a fail-safe stop, the hardware isolation boundary must encompass all computational, interconnect, and power resources required to execute the active recovery step. Just as the wheeled manipulator's placement record isolates the energy storage and gate drivers needed for powered braking, the biped's placement record must certify dedicated bus bandwidth, joint controller execution enclaves, and battery rail capacitance for active balance recovery.
:::

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-placement-fallacies-pitfalls}

Placement determines the physical resources shared by complex proposal algorithms and critical enforcement routines. Traces of normal operation cannot prove these systems are truly independent when rare physical events, such as power voltage transients, clock faults, memory contention, or a stalled producer, stress those shared hardware pathways.

```{python}
#| label: calc-placement-fallacy-margins
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ FALLACY MARGINS ON THE MACHINE'S PERMISSION TICK
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-placement-fallacies-pitfalls
# │
# │ Goal: Put the rail-droop and average-utilization fallacies on the machine's
# │       own enforcer budget.
# │ Show: the droop worked example's accelerator step stretches the modeled gate
# │       delay on the shared rail by about 39 percent, whatever the
# │       enforcer's privilege; a 320 µs read tail leaves 80 µs, less than
# │       the 95 µs that constraint evaluation and the drive-frame write need.
# │ How: Reuses InductivePDNVoltageDroop (the droop worked example) and
# │      PlacementMachine (registry fields and chapter-local sub-costs); the
# │      read tail is a scenario input.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim.core.units import microsecond, ureg
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_int, fmt_latency, check

class PlacementFallacyMargins:
    # ┌── 1. LOAD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    v_droop = InductivePDNVoltageDroop.v_droop  # category: derived (L dI/dt + I R)
    gate_stretch_pct = InductivePDNVoltageDroop.delay_expansion_pct  # category: derived (alpha-power model)
    deadline = PlacementMachine.deadline  # category: chosen (registry)
    compute_after_sense = PlacementMachine.compute_after_sense  # category: illustrative (80 + 15 µs)
    read_tail = 320 * microsecond  # scenario assumption; category: illustrative (shared-DRAM read tail)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    after_read = (deadline - read_tail).to(microsecond)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(v_droop.to(ureg.millivolt).magnitude - 138.0) < 1e-6, "90 mV inductive + 48 mV resistive = 138 mV of droop.")
    check(round(gate_stretch_pct) == 39, "The alpha-power model stretches gate delay by about 39 percent at 0.712 V.")
    check(after_read < compute_after_sense, "The read tail leaves less than the 95 µs of constraint and write work.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    gate_stretch_pct_str = fmt_int(round(gate_stretch_pct))
    deadline_str = fmt_latency(deadline, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    read_tail_str = fmt_latency(read_tail, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    after_read_str = fmt_latency(after_read, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    compute_after_sense_str = fmt_latency(compute_after_sense, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
```

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Logical privilege rings protect real-time enforcers from shared-rail electrical droop.*\index{Voltage droop!gate delay}\index{Interference!shared power rail}

Privilege checks govern digital access, while the rail supplies the gates that perform those checks. The illustrative droop calculation predicts a `{python} PlacementFallacyMargins.gate_stretch_pct_str` percent gate-delay increase under its stated model; only device characterization can determine the resulting setup margin or reset behavior. Lockstep cores sharing a rail can share a failure, so comparator coverage does not establish supply independence. The selected isolated rail removes one coupling path and still requires common-supply fault tests.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Sharing phase-locked loops or reset controllers across proposal and permission domains.*\index{Phase-locked loop!shared dependency}\index{Reset controller!isolation}

A separate core can still stop when a host-controlled reset asserts or slow when a shared governor changes its clock. The topology must trace each clock and reset to the controlling hardware, then test the relevant faults under load. Naming a controller a safety island does not establish that these dependencies are independent.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Low average memory bus utilization guarantees bounded read latency for real-time safety tasks.*\index{Memory bandwidth!worst-case execution time}\index{Tightly coupled memory}

Average utilization leaves the arrival order and longest queue unspecified. Plain FIFO queueing at the SoC's full bandwidth is not the danger, as notebook \ref{nbk-placement-loaded-read} showed; the read tail comes from an FR-FCFS controller that keeps passing the safety read in favor of a streaming accelerator's row hits, or from the miss-handling contention of @sec-placement-interference-mechanisms, and neither shows in an average. In an illustrative counterexample, such a tail stretches the snapshot read to `{python} PlacementFallacyMargins.read_tail_str`, which leaves `{python} PlacementFallacyMargins.after_read_str` before the `{python} PlacementFallacyMargins.deadline_str` deadline, less than the `{python} PlacementFallacyMargins.compute_after_sense_str` needed for evaluation and staging even before blocking and interference are charged. A service bound, qualified bypass, or independent local memory addresses that failure; a low average does not.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Using blocking software mutexes across inter-processor communication boundaries with untrusted neural policies.*\index{Mutex!inter-processor blocking}\index{Wait-free data structures!sequence locks}

A mutex held by a stalled proposer transfers control of the enforcement deadline to that proposer. An unbounded seqlock retry loop has the same defect when publication remains odd. The selected boundary protocol makes one read attempt per tick and discards a collision. That discard leaves an active valid command in force only while its own evidence, state, and lease remain admissible; it neither resets the lease nor forces premature revocation. Memory ordering and bounded copy time remain part of the placement evidence.

:::

## Summary {#sec-placement-summary}

Part I built the mobile manipulator on a hypothesis: its learned proposer runs on application processors and accelerators and its permission path on a bare-metal microcontroller\index{Microcontroller!bare-metal}. This chapter turned that hypothesis into a placement decision that evidence can refute. The allocation alone does not separate the two paths, because privilege boundaries govern none of the physical resources the two paths still share. Partitioning therefore requires a justified timing bound and fault evidence, with loaded tests able to refute the claim.

The evidence must cover the physical resources that the placement still shares. A loaded test supports a scoped claim about its workload, arbitration policy, supply, clock governance, and thermal conditions. Separate processor packages remove some coupling paths, but the board's common supply and communication links remain part of the argument. Across the link, the boundary contract keeps a stalled proposer from holding the permission deadline. The reader makes one bounded attempt per tick and discards a torn record, and a windowed watchdog trips on feeds that arrive too early as well as too late.

The placement record carries that evidence forward. It takes the permission path's declared worst-case execution time and deadline from the enforcement record and adds the loaded observed maxima for the declared test conditions, the shared-resource queue and power headroom, the common power, clock, reset, and memory failure paths, and the conditions left untested. The machine's own record holds a `{python} PlacementMachine.unloaded_str` illustrative unloaded estimate against the declared `{python} PlacementMachine.wcet_str` worst case inside the `{python} PlacementMachine.deadline_str` deadline and still awaits a loaded ledger, which must name the arbitration policy, clocks, sample count, and physical endpoint before any release claim can rest on it.

The observation contract, belief record, intent lease, trajectory record, enforcement record, and placement record now describe one machine. Its timing must hold across the chain, including the memory, power, and communication paths between stages. Placement makes the execution premise of principle \ref{pri-vol4-proposal-permission} falsifiable through a threshold, a stress campaign, and a record of what remains untested. Part IV inherits the conditional stopping margin, the unverified premise that aisle crossings are procedurally restricted (@sec-enforcement-composite-budget), the placement record's empty loaded field, and a dispatch-to-admission interval $\Delta_{\text{da}}$ that this chapter has allocated at `{python} PlacementTransport.delta_da_str`, inside the `{python} PlacementTransport.t_ceiling_str` the spare can pay for, but not yet measured.

Seven relations carry the chapter's quantitative argument, and @tbl-13-key-equations records each with the decision it settles and the place it is derived.

| Equation                                                                                                                                      | What it bounds or decides                                                                                                                         | Derived                               |
|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| $t_{\text{queue}} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{Q}} D_{\text{vol},k}/\text{BW}_{\text{peak}} + N_{\text{conflict}}(t_{\text{RP}} + t_{\text{RCD}})$  | How long a safety read waits behind a FIFO backlog on shared DRAM; a bound exists only if the controller limits the backlog or lets the read pass | @eq-placement-dram-queuing            |
| $f \le \dfrac{T_{\text{wcet}}/t_{\text{unloaded}} - 1}{r_{\text{slow}} - 1}$                                                                  | The largest share of the tick that may stall on shared-cache misses slowed by $r_{\text{slow}}$ before the loaded tick crosses the declared bound | @eq-placement-stall-share             |
| $\Delta V_{\text{droop}} = L_{\text{pkg}}\,dI/dt + \Delta I\,R_{\text{pkg}}$                                                                  | The first-order rail disturbance a current step imposes on a controller sharing its supply                                                        | @eq-placement-droop                   |
| $T_{\text{j}}(t) = T_{\text{j},\text{target}} + (T_{\text{j},\text{start}} - T_{\text{j},\text{target}})\,e^{-t/\tau_{\text{th}}}$            | How long a throttled clock persists after the load stops, and so how many ticks a shared thermal path exposes                                     | @eq-placement-cooling-recovery        |
| $\lvert T_{\text{feed}} - T_{\text{period}} \rvert \le (c_{\max} - c_{\min}) + J_{\text{phase}}$                                              | The service window a windowed watchdog must accept from a healthy tick, which sets its early trip and the floor for its late one                  | @eq-placement-watchdog-window         |
| $t_{\text{enf}} = t_{\text{iso}} + T_{\text{interf,shared}},\ t_{\text{iso}} \le T_{\text{wcet}} < T_{\text{deadline,enf}} < T_{\text{tick}}$ | The falsification threshold: a loaded cycle above $T_{\text{wcet}}$ refutes the placement's claim that proposal-side load adds no interference    | @eq-placement-falsification-threshold |
| $t_{\text{net}}^{\text{tail}} + t_{\text{proc}}^{\text{tail}} \le W$                                                                          | Whether an off-board result can renew the lease or become an admitted chunk                                                                       | @eq-placement-offload-window          |

: **Key equations of workload placement**: The relations behind the chapter's contention, thermal, supervision, falsification, and offload decisions, with the place each is derived. {#tbl-13-key-equations tbl-colwidths="[40,42,18]"}

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Silicon placement and memory contention"}
* **Logical separation is a hypothesis about hardware:** Privilege rings govern which addresses a task may touch, not where its requests wait, which rail feeds it, or which clock and reset tree it depends on. Loaded tests can refute the claim; justified bounds and fault evidence must support it.
* **Averages cannot bound a deadline, and bandwidth is not the main threat:** On a shared die at full bandwidth, more than `{python} PlacementLoadedRead.backlogs_wcet_str` FIFO backlogs must precede the snapshot read before it crosses the declared worst-case execution time. Shared-cache miss handling is far stronger: measured slowdowns of `{python} PlacementInterference.s_mshr_mult_str` and more than `{python} PlacementInterference.s_wb_mult_str` cross the declared bound once `{python} PlacementInterference.f_mshr_pct_str` or `{python} PlacementInterference.f_wb_pct_str` of the tick is miss stall. Only private memory or regulated co-runners bound that multiplier.
* **Couplings act on four timescales around a millisecond tick:** Rail droop acts in nanoseconds and interconnect queueing in microseconds, below the millisecond tick they threaten, while silicon thermal throttling persists for seconds after the load stops, and chassis structural and battery pack self-heating accumulates over multi-hour shifts. In the rejected shared-die placement, a halved clock stretches the enforcer's `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.wcet_str` cycle to `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.t_exec_throt_str` while inference runs and for `{python} RejectedPlacementThrottle.ticks_exposed_str` ticks after it stops.
* **The declared bound is the falsification threshold:** The declared worst-case execution time bounds the tick in isolation, and the selected placement claims that proposal-side load adds no interference term, so any loaded cycle above it refutes the placement's timing premise even when the deadline still holds. A passing trace supports only the states it tested.
* **A refuted claim forces a priced choice:** Regulation and reservation cost idle capacity, coloring and partitioning cost working set, workload reduction costs policy authority, and relocation adds a board link. On the machine that link costs `{python} PlacementTransport.t_link_str` of a `{python} PlacementTransport.delta_da_str` dispatch-to-admission allocation dominated by inference and validation.
* **Platform exposure is a placement constraint:** An on-die safety island with its own crystal, rail, and memory removes every die-level coupling except temperature, the reset chain, and the fabric its proposals cross, but as of 2026 the commercial modules that carry the machine's application processor do not enable it, so the permission path moves to a discrete controller.
* **The placement record bounds the deployment envelope:** It takes its declared worst-case execution time and deadline from the enforcement record and adds loaded observed maxima, thermal headroom, bus arbitration, mitigations, and untested conditions. On the mobile manipulator the measurement fields are still empty, so the independence claim reaches release review without loaded qualification evidence.
:::

Placement is where the third law becomes a property of hardware. Proposal is not permission only while the proposer cannot reach the permission decision through anything the two share, and on a real machine that includes memory, supply, clock, reset, and heat. The useful habit is to read every architecture diagram as a list of claims, one per shared resource, and to ask of each one what loaded measurement would refute it.

The running machine leaves Part III with a placement decision and an explicit evidence gap. The record names the resources that must preserve the permission deadline, the measurements that could refute their bounds, and the fallback that must remain available if the proposer fails. Governing the machine means judging such conditional claims, and the next proposer to claim authority will be a person.

## Historical Perspective and Further Reading {#sec-placement-history}

Avionics met the placement problem first. Once integrated modular avionics put functions of different criticality on one processor, the certifying question became whether a fault or overrun in one function could reach another, and @rushby1999partitioning separated the answer into two obligations: spatial partitioning, which protects memory and devices, and temporal partitioning, which protects the time each function is promised. The ARINC 653 interface turned the temporal half into fixed windows of a repeating frame, and @kopetz2011real built whole architectures on a global time base so that timing could be designed rather than discovered. Automotive practice later wrote the same concern into ISO 26262 as freedom from interference and dependent-failure analysis [@iso26262].

The bound itself had to be computed before it could be defended. @puschner1989calculating showed how to derive a maximum execution time from program structure, abstract interpretation [@cousot1977abstract] gave analyzers a sound way to model caches and pipelines, and implicit path enumeration [@li1995performance] turned the longest feasible path into an integer linear program. @wilhelm2008worst surveys the tools that combined them, while @lundqvist1999timing showed that local worst cases need not compose into a global one. @vestal2007preemptive then gave each task a budget per assurance level, the idea that lets a proposer overrun while an enforcer may not [@burns2017survey].

Multicore processors undid the single-core premise. Cores that share caches and memory controllers turn the memory wall [@wulf1995] from a throughput limit into a deadline problem, and the software answers followed in quick succession: phased execution that confines memory access to a separate phase [@pellizzoni2011predictable], per-core bandwidth regulation [@yun2013memguard], and bank-aware allocation [@yun2014palloc]. Measurements then showed that partitioning capacity leaves the miss-handling structures shared [@valsan2016taming; @bechtel2019denial], and certification caught up with AC 20-193 [@faa2024ac20193]. What this chapter adds is the physical side of the argument: the enforcer's bound is charged against a stopping distance, heat and supply couple the paths on timescales no scheduler sees, and the evidence travels to release in a placement record.

For further reading, six works trace the ideas this chapter composes.

- @rushby1999partitioning states the requirements for partitioning processors shared by functions of different criticality and separates the spatial and temporal obligations that the dependent-failure inventory of @tbl-13-placement-candidates checks row by row.
- @kopetz2011real develops real-time system design from a global time base, the discipline behind fixed ticks, deadlines, and time-triggered exchange.
- @wilhelm2008worst surveys static, measurement-based, and hybrid methods for worst-case execution time and the premises each rests on, the comparison behind @sec-placement-testing-separation.
- @burns2017survey reviews mixed-criticality scheduling from its origin to multicore platforms, the theory behind letting the proposer lose renewal while the permission tick survives.
- @yun2013memguard introduces per-core memory-bandwidth regulation, the mechanism that turns an unbounded interference multiplier on a shared die into a bounded one.
- @faa2024ac20193 is the current certification guidance for multicore processors, and it shows what a regulator requires before a shared-die timing bound can be believed.

## Problems {#sec-placement-problems}

```{python}
#| label: calc-placement-problems
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ END-OF-CHAPTER PROBLEM GIVENS
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-placement-problems
# │
# │ Goal: Load each problem's illustrative givens beside the chapter's own
# │       values and guard the property each problem depends on.
# │ Show: nine row conflicts or half bandwidth shrink the backlog budget; a 5
# │       percent stall share at 21x crosses the WCET but not the deadline; a
# │       4 ns rise halves the inductive droop; a 90 °C clear threshold halves
# │       the hangover; a doubled clock trips the watchdog's lower bound; a
# │       50 ms validation still fits the dispatch-to-admission ceiling; a
# │       32-cell campaign overruns a 40 h window; a humanoid's fall timescale
# │       is a seventh of the thermal hangover.
# │ How: chapter classes (PlacementMachine, PlacementLoadedRead,
# │      PlacementInterference, InductivePDNVoltageDroop,
# │      RejectedPlacementThrottle, PlacementTransport) and MLSysIM physics;
# │      every new given is illustrative and loaded here.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
import math
from mlsysim.core.units import ureg, microsecond, millisecond, second, meter, millimeter, nanosecond, hour, minute, millivolt
from mlsysim.physics import calc_partial_slowdown_stretch
from mlsysim.physics.robotics import (
    calc_axi_fifo_contention,
    calc_inductive_voltage_droop,
    calc_voltage_droop,
    calc_alpha_power_gate_delay_stretch,
    calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time,
    calc_watchdog_feed_window,
)
from mlsysim import Embodied
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_int, fmt_latency, fmt_length, fmt_multiple, fmt_percent, check

PM = PlacementMachine
LR = PlacementLoadedRead
DR = InductivePDNVoltageDroop
TH = RejectedPlacementThrottle
TR = PlacementTransport

class PlacementProblems:
    # ┌── 1. LOAD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    conflicts_p1 = 9  # category: illustrative (P1: tripled row conflicts)
    f_stall_p2 = 0.05  # category: illustrative (P2: measured stall share)
    t_rise_p3 = 4.0 * nanosecond  # category: illustrative (P3: slower current step)
    t_clear_p4 = 90.0  # °C; category: illustrative (P4: raised clearance threshold)
    c_min_p5 = 60 * microsecond  # category: illustrative (P5: shortest completion)
    j_phase_p5 = 20 * microsecond  # category: illustrative (P5: inter-tick jitter bound)
    t_validate_p6 = 50 * millisecond  # category: illustrative (P6: heavier admission check)
    n_factors_p7 = 5  # category: chosen (P7: two-level factors)
    n_ticks_p7 = 10_000_000  # category: chosen (P7: ticks per cell)
    window_p7 = 40 * hour  # category: illustrative (P7: test window)
    loaded_max_p8 = 231 * microsecond  # category: illustrative (P8: campaign maximum)
    unloaded_max_p8 = 142 * microsecond  # category: illustrative (P8: unloaded maximum)
    z_c_p9 = (
        Embodied.Humanoid.Unitree_H1.com_height
    )  # category: illustrative (P9: humanoid CoM height; registry estimate, as in @sec-nervous-coupled-budget)
    p999_p10 = 180 * microsecond  # category: illustrative (P10: vendor P99.9)
    n_ticks_p10 = 1_000_000  # category: illustrative (P10: vendor trace length)
    util_p11 = 0.30  # category: illustrative (P11: average LPDDR utilization)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def _backlogs(bandwidth, conflicts):
        r = calc_axi_fifo_contention(
            tile_bytes=LR.tile_bytes,
            camera_bytes=LR.camera_bytes,
            telemetry_bytes=LR.telemetry_bytes,
            safety_read_bytes=LR.snapshot_bytes,
            transaction_bytes=LR.transaction_bytes,
            bandwidth=bandwidth,
            bank_switches=conflicts,
            bank_switch_time=LR.bank_switch_time,
            compute_time=LR.compute_after_sense,
        )
        q, o = r["queue_fifo"], r["own_read"]
        n = lambda ceiling: math.floor(((ceiling - o) / q).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
        return q.to(microsecond), n(LR.sense), n(LR.wcet_read_ceiling), n(LR.read_ceiling)

    q_p1a, ns_p1a, nw_p1a, nd_p1a = _backlogs(LR.bandwidth, conflicts_p1)
    q_p1b, ns_p1b, nw_p1b, nd_p1b = _backlogs(LR.bandwidth / 2, LR.bank_switches)
    s_wcet_p2 = 1 + (PlacementInterference.stretch_wcet - 1) / f_stall_p2
    s_dl_p2 = 1 + (PlacementInterference.stretch_deadline - 1) / f_stall_p2
    t_21_p2 = (PM.unloaded * calc_partial_slowdown_stretch(f_stall_p2, PlacementInterference.s_mshr)).to(microsecond)
    v_ind_p3 = calc_inductive_voltage_droop(DR.l_pkg, DR.delta_i / t_rise_p3).to(millivolt)
    v_res_p3 = calc_voltage_droop(DR.delta_i, DR.r_pkg).to(millivolt)
    v_droop_p3 = (v_ind_p3 + v_res_p3).to(millivolt)
    stretch_p3 = calc_alpha_power_gate_delay_stretch(
        nominal_voltage=DR.v_core, drooped_voltage=DR.v_core - v_droop_p3, threshold_voltage=DR.v_th, alpha=DR.alpha
    )["delay_expansion_percent"]
    t_recov_p4 = (TH.tau_th * math.log((TH.t_start - TH.t_target) / (t_clear_p4 - TH.t_target))).to(second)
    ticks_p4 = math.floor((t_recov_p4 / PM.tick).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    theta_max_p4 = (TH.t_start - TH.t_ambient) / TH.p_load
    window_p5 = calc_watchdog_feed_window(PM.tick, c_min_p5, PM.wcet, j_phase_p5)  # @eq-placement-watchdog-window
    spread_p5 = window_p5["spread"]
    t_lower_p5 = window_p5["t_lower"]
    t_upper_p5 = window_p5["t_upper"]
    t_fast_p5 = (PM.tick / 2).to(microsecond)
    d_timeout_p5 = (TR.v_aisle * PM.self_watchdog).to(millimeter)
    period_max_p6 = (PM.lease - PM.renewal_jitter).to(millisecond)
    delta_da_p6 = (TR.delta_da - TR.t_validate + t_validate_p6).to(millisecond)
    reserve_p6 = (TR.t_ceiling - delta_da_p6).to(millisecond)
    reserve_d_p6 = (TR.v_aisle * reserve_p6).to(millimeter)
    validate_max_p6 = (TR.t_ceiling - (TR.delta_da - TR.t_validate)).to(millisecond)
    cells_p7 = 2**n_factors_p7
    t_cell_p7 = (n_ticks_p7 * PM.tick).to(hour)
    t_full_p7 = (cells_p7 * t_cell_p7).to(hour)
    ticks_half_p7 = math.floor((window_p7 / (cells_p7 // 2) / PM.tick).to("dimensionless").magnitude)
    margin_wcet_p8 = (PM.wcet - loaded_max_p8).to(microsecond)
    t_fall_p9 = calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time(effective_length=z_c_p9).to(millisecond)
    ratio_p9 = (TH.t_recov / t_fall_p9).to("dimensionless").magnitude
    growth_p9 = math.exp(ratio_p9)
    t_trace_p10 = (n_ticks_p10 * PM.tick).to(minute)
    n_above_p10 = round(n_ticks_p10 * 0.001)
    rate_hr_p10 = (3 / n_ticks_p10) * (hour / PM.tick).to("dimensionless").magnitude

    # ┌── 3. GUARD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    check((ns_p1a, nw_p1a, nd_p1a) == (18, 73, 102), "P1: nine conflicts leave 18, 73, 102 backlogs (deadline under the full response budget).")
    check((ns_p1b, nw_p1b, nd_p1b) == (10, 42, 58), "P1: half bandwidth leaves 10, 42, 58 backlogs (deadline under the full response budget).")
    check(s_wcet_p2 < PlacementInterference.s_mshr < s_dl_p2, "P2: 21x crosses the WCET but not the deadline at 5 percent.")
    check(PM.wcet < t_21_p2 < PM.exec_ceiling, "P2: the tick lands between the WCET and the deadline less blocking and interference.")
    check(abs(v_ind_p3.magnitude - 45.0) < 1e-6 and abs(v_res_p3.magnitude - 48.0) < 1e-6, "P3: 45 mV inductive, 48 mV resistive.")
    check(stretch_p3 < DR.delay_expansion_pct, "P3: the slower step stretches gate delay less.")
    check(ticks_p4 == 1014 and theta_max_p4 < TH.theta_ja, "P4: 1,014 ticks at 90 °C; the scenario's resistance exceeds the no-trip limit.")
    check(
        abs(t_lower_p5.magnitude - 790.0) < 1e-6 and abs(t_upper_p5.magnitude - 1210.0) < 1e-6,
        f"P5: feed window drifted: [{t_lower_p5}, {t_upper_p5}]",
    )
    check(abs(z_c_p9.to(meter).magnitude - 0.9) < 1e-9, f"P9: humanoid CoM height drifted: {z_c_p9}")
    check(
        t_fast_p5 < t_lower_p5 and PM.self_watchdog > t_upper_p5,
        "P5: a doubled clock trips the lower bound; the 5 ms timeout sits beyond the window.",
    )
    check(TR.delta_da < TR.t_ceiling and delta_da_p6 < TR.t_ceiling, "P6: the heavier validation still fits the ceiling.")
    check(
        t_full_p7 > window_p7 and ticks_half_p7 < n_ticks_p7, "P7: the full factorial overruns the window, and so does a half fraction at 10^7 ticks."
    )
    check(loaded_max_p8 < PM.wcet and unloaded_max_p8 < loaded_max_p8, "P8: the illustrative campaign passes.")
    check(ratio_p9 > 7 and TH.ticks_exposed > 2000, "P9: the hangover spans more than seven fall timescales.")
    check(abs(rate_hr_p10 - 10.8) < 1e-9, "P10: 3e-6 per tick at 1 kHz is 10.8 per hour.")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    conflicts_p1_str = fmt_int(conflicts_p1)
    f_stall_p2_pct_str = fmt_percent(f_stall_p2, precision=0, style="prose")
    t_rise_p3_str = fmt(t_rise_p3.to(nanosecond).magnitude, precision=0)
    t_clear_p4_str = fmt(t_clear_p4, precision=0)
    c_min_p5_str = fmt_latency(c_min_p5, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    j_phase_p5_str = fmt_latency(j_phase_p5, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    t_validate_p6_str = fmt_latency(t_validate_p6, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    n_factors_p7_str = fmt_int(n_factors_p7)
    window_p7_str = fmt(window_p7.to(hour).magnitude, precision=0)
    loaded_max_p8_str = fmt_latency(loaded_max_p8, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    unloaded_max_p8_str = fmt_latency(unloaded_max_p8, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    z_c_p9_str = fmt_length(z_c_p9, unit=meter, precision=1)
    p999_p10_str = fmt_latency(p999_p10, unit=microsecond, precision=0)
    util_p11_pct_str = fmt_percent(util_p11, precision=0, style="prose")
```

Each problem states its givens, which come from the running machine's registry values, the chapter's own calculations, or the problem itself. A given marked illustrative is an assumption for the exercise, not a measurement. The tag names the kind of work, and the parenthesis names the learning objective the problem assesses.

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From compute placement to intervention"}
What happens to the stopping budget when the slowest delay belongs to a person? Every delay this chapter examined belonged to the machine (a queued read, a stretched gate, a throttled clock), and each one can be bounded or refuted by a test on the chassis. @Sec-intervention opens Part IV with a delay that no placement can bound. A remote assistant who takes over the mobile manipulator in an aisle introduces response delay beyond the machine intervals considered here, over a link the permission path does not control, and that reaction spends the same stopping budget. The right to propose must then pass between the learned proposer and a person while the permission path keeps checking every command from both, the handover must not itself produce the motion it was meant to prevent, and every tick must record who held that right.
:::
